clue.text: NEWS in brief

parts.note: read the capitals N, E, W and S as short forms, each the abbreviation of a compass point

explanation.surface: A request for a summary of the day's headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals give the game away: NEWS is not tidings but the four compass-point letters, each an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: N, E, W and S are the abbreviated compass points, the ways one can head.

clue.text: Anything but happy working in refuse tips

explanation.surface: A gloomy worker at the rubbish heap.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse tips are rubbish dumps, so someone working at one is literally low down among them; the idiom means miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone depressed and gloomy; taken literally it places a person at a rubbish heap.

clue.text: Ugh, actors can be so crude when plastered

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words can be made into something else, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that theatre folk get coarse when drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' suggests drunkenness, but it means coated with plaster: a wall finished with a coarse pebbly render.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough-textured exterior render of lime and gravel gives a coarse plastered finish.

clue.text: Cried out for refreshment

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone yelled for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A fermented apple drink is a common refreshment.

clue.text: State of an allotment in the subcontinent

annotationWithheld.why: 'State of an allotment in the subcontinent' (7) gives INDIAN + A at best; no parse found for 'allotment' supplying letters or acting as an indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: State of an allotment in the subcontinent

clue.text: Recalling an aroma coming into being

indicators.note: calling back suggests the little word an is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: an aroma is a scent

explanation.surface: Someone remembering a smell as it first arises.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just emerging and beginning to develop is newborn or incipient.

clue.text: Leading character on the staff

parts.note: the staff is the musical stave, and the first symbol written on it fixes the pitch of its lines

explanation.surface: The chief figure among an organisation's employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but it is the five-line musical stave; the symbol at its start is the leading character.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble or bass sign is printed first on every musical stave to fix pitches.

clue.text: Curry favour in the corridor

explanation.surface: Someone sucking up to people in a hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: To petition politicians is to seek influence, and an entrance hall or corridor bears the same name.

clue.text: Safety curtain, say

parts.note: a theatre's safety curtain is one example of a barrier against flames

explanation.surface: An example of the protective drop in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's safety curtain is a barrier lowered to stop flames spreading, as a hearth guard does at home.

clue.text: Range of a number in character-forming styles

indicators.note: in places the number inside the writing instruments

parts.note: styles, or styluses, are pens: instruments that form written characters
nine is a number

explanation.surface: A mountain range belonging to a set of fashions in handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: A style is an old word for a stylus or pen, the tool that forms written characters.
explanation.definitionFit: The hills running down northern England form a mountain range, often called its backbone.

clue.text: Bound to hurt one's feelings …

explanation.surface: Someone sure to cause offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound means wrapped round, as a bandage is; the same word for an injury means to offend or upset.

clue.text: … to do so in such a cutting way

definitions.text: … to do so in such a cutting way

parts.words: to do so in such a cutting way
parts.note: continuing the previous clue: to injure by actually cutting a body apart limb from limb

explanation.surface: Hurting someone's feelings with a particularly sharp remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like a sarcastic remark, but taken literally it means slicing someone into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut off limbs is to injure in the most literally cutting way.

clue.text: The ship's due at one stage or another

definitions.text: The ship's due at one stage or another

parts.words: The ship's due at one stage or another
parts.note: a landing stage is a quay, and a ship owes a fee for berthing at one

explanation.surface: A vessel will arrive at some point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Due' looks like expected arrival and 'stage' like a time; in fact due is a charge and stage is a landing stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The charge levied on a vessel for using a quay or landing stage.

clue.text: Contradictory linesman?

parts.note: a negative followed by a positive is a contradictory pair of replies
a negative followed by a positive is a contradictory pair of replies

explanation.surface: A football official who argues back.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'linesman' here is a writer of lines of verse: Alfred Noyes, English poet of 'The Highwayman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English poet, a writer of lines of verse.

clue.text: See 1 down
Falls back once more on the artist

indicators.note: back tells us to read the synonym for once more in reverse

parts.note: once more means again
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone collapses again onto a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Lilacs he ordered for a Paris victim

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man buying flowers for someone hurt in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is not the French capital but the Trojan prince whose arrow struck the Greek hero's heel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero was killed by the Trojan prince Paris with an arrow to his heel.

clue.text: Crazy tear about beast gets the bird

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the animal
crazy tells us the letters of tear are jumbled

parts.note: a nag is a horse, a beast

explanation.surface: A wild tearaway animal gets jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges TEAR to TA...ER, which goes 'about' NAG. 'Gets the bird' looks like being booed, but the bird is the definition: a brightly coloured American songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly coloured American songbird of the finch family.

clue.text: Where Galatea became involved with a male leader outside the youth centre

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
became involved suggests the letters get tangled up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Asks where the statue-woman Galatea got entangled with a man in charge outside a youth club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Became involved' anagrams GALATEA plus M (male's leader) into GATEMALA, which goes 'outside' U, the centre of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American country is a place, so it answers the question where.

clue.text: Restraints for couples

explanation.surface: Restraints used on pairs of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Knots and tethers that hold are restraints; to hook up or attach a trailer is to couple it.

clue.text: Outlook for many living at the coast

definitions.text: Outlook for many living at the coast

parts.words: Outlook for many living at the coast
parts.note: the outlook is the vista from a window rather than a forecast

explanation.surface: Prospects for seaside residents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlook' suggests a forecast of prospects, but it is literally what seaside residents see from their windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Homes by the shore look out over the water, a scene of waves.

clue.text: Sanguine about Teresa getting in around

indicators.note: getting in means the round letter is placed inside the jumbled name
about signals that Teresa's letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: a ring shape, a round, is the letter O

explanation.surface: Being cheerful concerning Teresa arriving nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanguine' looks like optimistic, but here it means blood-red or rosy in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine can mean blood-red or ruddy, and this word means rosy pink.

clue.text: Mrs. Ruff left one inside to give solace

indicators.note: inside places the two letters within the female bird

parts.note: the female of the ruff, a wading bird, is called a reeve
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruff departed, leaving a person within to comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs. Ruff looks like a person, but she is the wife of the ruff, a wading bird; the female is a reeve.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease someone's distress is to comfort or console them.

clue.text: Lived to recall a fighting spirit

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone survived to remember a combative attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighting spirit' looks like determination; here it is an evil spirit, a demon at war with good.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon or evil spirit, Satan's kind, battles against goodness.

clue.text: Imprecise number with acute fever

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five, a number
ague is a fever with shivering fits

explanation.surface: Inaccurate figures accompanying a sharp fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclear or ill-defined is a synonym of imprecise.

clue.text: Ship's company in a state of confusion?

explanation.surface: A crew in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole crew is out on the ocean; the idiom means bewildered.

clue.text: Square-bashing suit for an emperor

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's square, giving T

indicators.note: bashing knocks the letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: A military drill outfit fit for a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Square-bashing is British slang for parade-ground drill, but here it splits into T (square) and 'bashing' as the anagram signal for SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Roman emperor of the first century AD.

clue.text: Like a man who won at Wimbledon

parts.note: as means like
he is a male pronoun, a man

explanation.surface: Similar to a men's champion of the tennis tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ashe, American tennis player, won the Wimbledon singles title in 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe was the American player who took the Wimbledon men's singles title in 1975.

clue.text: Display charisma when a meeting's arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: meeting's stands for meeting is, giving the letters with S

explanation.surface: Being charming once a get-together is fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract people as a magnet does iron is to show charisma.

clue.text: Operatic heroine of the natives

explanation.surface: An opera's lead character being one of the locals.
explanation.definitionFit: Massenet's opera is named after its courtesan heroine; natives of Thailand share the name.

clue.text: Staunch supporter

explanation.surface: A loyal backer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stanch a flow is to stop it; a plant's stalk holds up its flower or leaf.

clue.text: Cries in the post-very chancy

indicators.note: in places the crying inside the post

parts.note: a stake is a post
weeps means cries

explanation.surface: Tears over a letter in the mail, an uncertain business.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a lottery on a race is a very chancy thing, where winning depends on drawn tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep is a lottery where prizes go by chance draw, so it is a thing of pure luck.
